newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis groups affirm confidence in TWA.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis groups affirm confidence in TWA.

text.p: Civic and business groups in St. Louis affirmed their confidence in Trans World Airlines Inc after the company said auditors plan to qualify the carrier's 1996 year end financial results.

Richard Fleming, president and chief executive officer of the St. Louis Regional Commerce and Growth Association, said that while the group recognizes TWA faces "difficult challenges," progress has been made.

"Based on our review and conversations with (TWA) chairman Gerald Gitner, we are confident, especially with the strong steps recently taken to deal with operational deficiencies," Fleming said in a statement Thursday. "TWA's new management has taken a hard-nosed approach necessary if the airline is going to be competitive."
Civic Progress, a group of top business executives in the region, said it also did its own third-party evaluation of the airline.

William Maritz, the group's president, said in a statement that the report pointed to little risk in the financial commitment the group's members had made in the airline through the advance purchase of $26 million in tickets.
Earlier this month, the group announced that 20 member companies decided to support TWA by prepurchasing up to six months of advance tickets on the airline, worth $26 million.
Both groups underscored the importance of TWA to its hub Lambert-St. Louis International Airport, where a $1.88 billion expansion plan is awaiting Federal Aviation Administration approval.
The FAA is scheduled to release an environmental impact statement for the project in late spring or early summer, followed by a record of decision in late summer, according to an FAA spokesman.

The statements by the civic leaders were released after the airline said the opinion of its independent auditors regarding its 1996 results will include a qualification regarding TWA's ability to continue as a going concern.

The exact wording of the qualification by KPMG Peat Marwick LLP will not be released until the company's 1996 annual report is filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission by March 31, according to the company.
